# First toy chapter {#sec-first}

For inline mathematics, let $z=x+y$. The labelled display

$$
x+y=z
$$ {#eq-seed}

will be cited from the next chapter.

::: {#def-seed}
## Seed definition

A *toy seed* is a pair $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$.
:::

::: {#thm-seed}
## Seed theorem

Every toy seed satisfies:

(a) []{#seed-item-a} $x+0=x$;

(b) []{#seed-item-b} $y+0=y$.
:::

[]{#proof-seed}

::: {.proof}
Both statements are the additive identity law. This proof has an explicit
ordinary identifier, so it can be reached by this [proof link](#proof-seed).
:::

::: {#lem-balance}
## Balance lemma

The following aligned identity holds:

$$
\begin{aligned}
(x+y)^2 &= x^2+2xy+y^2,\\
(x-y)^2 &= x^2-2xy+y^2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-balance}
:::

::: {#prp-forms}
## Forms proposition

Matrix and cases notation render together:

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
f(t)=\begin{cases}t,&t\ge 0,\\-t,&t<0.\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-forms}
:::

::: {#exm-seed}
## Seed example

The pair $(1,2)$ is a toy seed.
:::

## Forward-reference remark
